resources.string: Traffic may leak. This prototype supports TCP only; UDP, calls and some apps may not work. Do not rely on it for sensitive activity. A new Tor identity does not guarantee a different exit IP.
Connection state is reported by the local VPN service.
Testing may reconnect the tunnel. Availability depends on your network; bypass is never guaranteed.

Real speed testing requires the separately installed Routeveil Probe helper, signed with the same certificate. Without it, the main VPN still works, but fastest-transport testing is unavailable. The service will check for the helper.\n\nThe test contacts check.torproject.org and speed.cloudflare.com through Tor. It tests up to 4 profiles × 64 KiB, plus Tor bootstrap traffic and protocol overhead. Switching profiles interrupts existing connections. Proceed?
Automatic prefers the transport in supplied bridge lines, otherwise Snowflake. Direct Tor still uses Tor; it is not the per-app DIRECT setting.
Bridge lines are stored locally exactly as entered, including whitespace and line breaks. They are not uploaded by this screen. obfs4 and WebTunnel need valid bridge lines.

Checked apps bypass Tor and expose their network connections to your ISP. HTTPS still protects encrypted content. Android “Block connections without VPN” (lockdown) blocks these apps instead of letting them go direct.

The initial list is an editable convenience preset, NOT an official operator whitelist: Госуслуги (ru.gosuslugi.gosuslugi), Яндекс Навигатор (ru.yandex.yandexnavi), Яндекс Go (ru.yandex.taxi), VK (com.vkontakte.android), MAX (ru.oneme.app). It does not promise access during restrictions.
None — no apps selected for direct access.

Only visible installed apps with a launcher and Internet permission are listed. Package IDs identify each app. Unlisted selections are retained. Routeveil and Routeveil Probe cannot be excluded. Changes apply on reconnect.
No visible launchable Internet apps were found.
Could not load the app list.
Saving does not change a running tunnel. Disconnect and reconnect to apply transport, bridges, rotation and DIRECT app changes. Connect and transport testing also save these settings.

Rotating a Tor identity does not itself require a CAPTCHA. If a website asks for one, solve it in the same app and session that opened that website; solving it here or in another browser does not transfer that session.\n\nThe official bridges.torproject.org site may ask you to complete a challenge to obtain a bridge. Routeveil does not detect or automatically solve CAPTCHAs. A browser opens only after you tap a link button.
The service supplied an approved Tor Project HTTPS link. You may open it from CAPTCHA help.
Link blocked: only HTTPS on bridges.torproject.org or check.torproject.org is allowed.
No app is available to open this HTTPS link.
VPN permission was not granted. Nothing was connected.
Notifications are disabled. Android may still show the VPN in its active-apps controls.
Could not send the request to the VPN service.
Android could not prepare the VPN. Check other VPNs and device policy.
Request sent to the VPN service.
Fixed technical event codes are kept locally in two rotating logs of up to 128 KiB each. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

Create a report and choose where to send it? It contains UTC event times, fixed technical event codes, Android SDK and app version; timestamps can reveal when you used the VPN. The text report is at most 300 KiB.\n\nExcluded: IP addresses, URLs, bridge lines, identifiers, installed-app lists, messages, network contents, logcat and native logs. Only this snapshot is shared, not future live logs. No automatic upload occurs. The recipient you choose can keep a copy.

Delete both local diagnostic logs and the exported report? This does not change VPN settings or disconnect it. A running service may record new events afterwards. Copies already sent to other apps cannot be recalled.
Could not prepare or clear diagnostics. No data was sent.
No app is available to share the diagnostic report.
